sentences.text: John, Melissa. Good to see you both today.
Hello Dr Chan.
Hello Dr Chan.
Good to see you.
all right let’s get started.
As you know, the purpose of this meeting is to discuss the preparations for the Asian Games Week in October and the the Wellness Month in July.
John, have we decided on the slogan for the Asian Games Week yet?
Not yet Dr Chan, no, but I'd like to start preparing the marketing for the event soon, so Im open to suggestions for the slogan.
How about. Passion, Pride, Performance.
Those Those are the values of the Asian Games, are they not?
They are, but I was thinking we could just use the official slogan of the Asian Games.
That would work too, Melissa.
What's the slogan?
It’s One Games, One Asia Is that written One Games comma, One Asia That’s right: there’s a comma in between One Games and One Asia
Powerful. It'll look very good on the poster.
OK, so we're going with One Games, One Asia then?
Absolutely. Sounds good.
Right. After the slogan, the next item on the agenda is the opening event of the Asian Games Week.
week. What needs to be decided?
Well, first things first: have we decided on a date yet?
we were currently considering the sixth or the thirteenth of October.
Either of those would be fine.
I’m sure earlier is better for the students, though.
Shall we go with the sixth?
Wait: um, isn’t the seventh the public holiday?
Let me check.
Oh yes, you’re right.
Let’s start the Asian Games Week on the 13th of October, then.
OK, OK, got it.
The 13th. Melissa, you were thinking of inviting someone to come speak at the school, is that right?
Do you think that'll take a whole day?
Yes, that’s the plan, but no: I don’t think it'll take a whole day.
It can be just an afternoon.
Is the event indoors or outdoors?
Well, the weather in October is generally quite good, so I did think about holding it in the sports ground.
To be safe, though, we'd better hold it in the Main Hall. We never know what the skies will bring.
sentences.timingMethod: Official script, sentence bounds corroborated by local ASR; no invented word timing

sentences.text: I agree. Hold it in the Main Hall.
Better safe than sorry.
We're holding some of the events of the Wellness Month and the Main Hall as well, aren’t we?
That's right, but the Wellness Month starts in July.
It won't affect the Asian Games Week in October.
Sure I just meant it’s a reliable venue for big school events, that’s all.
Speaking of the Wellness Month, what theme are we using this year?
I was actually thinking of using the theme of hiking for this year’s Wellness Month since we haven’t done that theme yet.
Hiking? In July?
I’m happy for us to have a few outdoor events, but I think it’s much too hot for hiking then.
The Wellness Month is just after the students finish their exams.
How about a theme of, Relax and Recover Do the students really need to recover after their exams?
The teachers, maybe.
I think Melissa’s right, John.
Relax and Recover fits in well with this part of the school year.
Let’s go with that.
OK, Dr Chan, if you say so.
Actually, that’s a pretty good idea, Melissa.
I remember that last year’s Yoga and Meditation sessions were a big hit with students.
students. We should run these again this year.
Yes, we should, and they fit the theme as well.
Perhaps we can focus on another benefit of Yoga this time, though, when we do the promotion.
Which benefit is that?
What most people don’t know is that Yoga can improve your focus and attention span.
That’s a great selling point.
I know plenty of students who struggle with this, so if this event can help them out with that, all the better.
Excellent. Mention this benefit when we promote the Yoga and Meditation sessions.
I also remember that the event was so popular last year because of the celebrity Yoga instructors.
chapters, Having not one, but two famous instructors was a huge hit!
Melissa, could you invite them again this year?
I can. I know a few people who'd love to help out, but we can’t use their names just yet until they’ve confirmed.
I can get two famous instructors for sure, though.
Excellent. Excellent. Put that in the marketing as well, John.
Ah, speaking of invitations, we've missed an agenda item about the Asian Games Week.
Oh, which one?
Well, just now we didn’t finish discussing who we're inviting to the opening event of the Asian Games Week, Melissa was just about to tell us who we're inviting to be our guest speaker.
Was I? I don’t have a name for that yet.
any ideas? Well, the Asian Games are adding new sports all the time.
For the opening event of the The Asian Games Week, maybe we can invite an athlete who represents an interesting sport?
I like the sound of that.
They could talk about why they think their sport should be added to the Asian Games.
Good idea, John.
It would be fascinating to hear an athlete give reasons for why their sport should be added to the Asian Games.
I know: how about I set up a survey to see which sports our students would be most interested in hearing about?
Sounds good. Actually, can we try to get our students even more involved in the Asian Games Week?
How can we make the event How about holding a discussion about the sport after the guest speaker has finished their speech?
I agree: holding a discussion about the sport would be a great way for our students to learn more.
Exactly. Make sure there is some time given to students to ask questions to make it really interactive.
John, can you handle this?
Yes, sure, I'll make sure there’s plenty of time for students to ask questions after the guest speaker’s speech.
OK, back to the Wellness Month.
There are a few more things we need to talk about.
We're definitely going to need some help once the Wellness Month begins.
ends. Melissa, I remember last year we had some parents involved in the events, yes, that’s right, though I don’t quite remember exactly what their responsibilities were.
I'll get in touch with Mr Singh on the Events Team to check our records and see what responsibilities the parents had.
I remember that parents were asked to attend a briefing session last year before they could help out.
Yes, perhaps we can have a similar arrangement this year.
It was definitely useful for them to take part in.
Sure, we can arrange that.
I do remember, though, it was a bit difficult to get parents to sign up.
Actually, how should parents sign up?
How should they show their interest in being involved?
They can sign up on the school website.
No, through the school app.
Ah yes, of course.
Through the app.
How are we planning to get more parents involved this year, then?
We thought a letter from one of the students would be effective in persuading them, especially once they hear about all the benefits.
Do you have someone in mind?
I’m going to ask Nico Lin, president of the Healthy Living Club, to write the letter.
Nico is also helping us out with a few other tasks related to the Wellness Month, as well as the Asian Games Week.
That sounds like good experience for Nico.
Niko, give Niko the recording of today's meeting.
We've made quite a few decisions about these two events today.
OK, I'll be sure to.
I think we’ve covered everything we need to for now.
Thank you both, Let’s keep in touch as things progress.
Speak soon, Dr.
Chan. on. See you later.

scoringPoints.referenceAnswer: the Asian Games was first held in 1951
Hangzhou, Incheon and Doha have all hosted the Games
long-distance running, chess and e-sports are three sports that have featured
Mascots: in Hangzhou / 2022 the mascots were three futuristic robot characters
in Nagoya / 2026 the mascot will be a tigerfish, which means ‘flame’ in Japanese
to promote environmental awareness, the organisers (of Incheon 2014) collected rainwater for the athletes / participants
to promote health awareness, (in Nagoya 2026) there will be a “walk for fun” campaign
to get the public walking more
Hong Kong won 53 medals at the last Asian Games / in Hangzhou / in 2022
